sources.title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.population_design_dose: 43 controlled studies; healthy adults; supervised concurrent training >=4 weeks vs identical strength alone. Chronic strength, explosive strength and hypertrophy, not next-morning readiness.
sources.findings: Pooled maximal strength and hypertrophy did not show clear attenuation; explosive-strength attenuation was present, especially close/session combinations. No universal compatibility or spacing claim follows.
sources.locator: Abstract Methods/Results; Discussion sections on explosive strength and limitations; publisher lines185-214.
limitations: Mostly medium/low methodological quality; intensity not consistently reported
Active training status pooled broadly; chronic group estimates cannot identify acute individual adequacy
counterevidence: L04 finds endpoint/subgroup attenuation under different definitions
No order-specific pooled effect established here; same-session power exception matters

sources.title: Acute Neuromuscular, Physiological and Performance Responses After Strength Training in Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: de Carvalho e Silva GI et al.
sources.population_design_dose: 19 qualitative/13 meta-analyzed studies of runners after resistance exercise; heterogeneous strength protocols, tasks and assessment times.
sources.findings: Acute peak torque and subjective/muscle-damage measures could worsen while several submaximal running physiological outcomes showed little change. Task and dose matter.
sources.locator: Results; Discussion including protocol contrasts; limitations and practical implications, publisher lines198-211.
limitations: Too few studies for robust 6/10/24/48h recovery curve
Does not quantify cost of the exact squat/RDL/split or guarantee a reduced set restores performance
counterevidence: Some submaximal tasks not impaired; reducing every lower/run pairing is unjustified
No single protocol result can define all runners time-to-recovery

sources.title: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
sources.population_design_dose: 137 systematic reviews of randomized healthy-adult RT interventions,6-52 weeks; literature search October2024. General strength, hypertrophy, function and power outcomes.
sources.findings: Progressive RT with goal-specific variables is supported; many configurations work. Failure is not necessary; exact optimal set counts and individual response cannot be read from pooled summaries.
sources.locator: Eligibility; Tables3/6; Discussion and limitations lines900-924. Full text newly available in this round, unlike pilot abstract access.
limitations: Review overlap quantified only for strength; variable-level overview not comparison of all compound programs
Group-level general adult evidence does not certify an individual dose, clinical clearance, or specialized concurrent/taper program
counterevidence: More volume may improve some outcomes; omitted work is not assumed equivalent
Specificity and goal change can make a convenient substitute inadequate

sources.title: Concurrent Strength and Endurance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on the Impact of Sex and Training Status
sources.authors: Huiberts RO, Wust RCI, van der Zwaard S
sources.population_design_dose: 59 studies/1346 healthy adults18-50, concurrent >=4 weeks; strength/endurance training status classified separately. Online2023, issue2024.
sources.findings: Subgroup and outcome-specific attenuation qualifies universal no-interference claims. Highly strength-trained populations were absent; female hypertrophy data sparse.
sources.locator: Methods2.2-2.6; Results3.1/3.4/3.5; Discussion.
limitations: Mostly untrained strength participants; limited highly trained endurance evidence
Subgroup association does not select acute action from sex or prove female safety
counterevidence: Different definitions and endpoints fromL01; no vote-counting or same-PICO contradiction invented
Not an individual prediction or automatic priority policy

sources.title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.population_design_dose: 43 controlled studies; healthy adults; supervised concurrent training >=4 weeks vs identical strength alone. Chronic strength, explosive strength and hypertrophy, not next-morning readiness.
sources.findings: Pooled maximal strength and hypertrophy did not show clear attenuation; explosive-strength attenuation was present, especially close/session combinations. No universal compatibility or spacing claim follows.
sources.locator: Abstract Methods/Results; Discussion sections on explosive strength and limitations; publisher lines185-214.
limitations: Mostly medium/low methodological quality; intensity not consistently reported
Active training status pooled broadly; chronic group estimates cannot identify acute individual adequacy
counterevidence: L04 finds endpoint/subgroup attenuation under different definitions
No order-specific pooled effect established here; same-session power exception matters

sources.title: Acute Neuromuscular, Physiological and Performance Responses After Strength Training in Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: de Carvalho e Silva GI et al.
sources.population_design_dose: 19 qualitative/13 meta-analyzed studies of runners after resistance exercise; heterogeneous strength protocols, tasks and assessment times.
sources.findings: Acute peak torque and subjective/muscle-damage measures could worsen while several submaximal running physiological outcomes showed little change. Task and dose matter.
sources.locator: Results; Discussion including protocol contrasts; limitations and practical implications, publisher lines198-211.
limitations: Too few studies for robust 6/10/24/48h recovery curve
Does not quantify cost of the exact squat/RDL/split or guarantee a reduced set restores performance
counterevidence: Some submaximal tasks not impaired; reducing every lower/run pairing is unjustified
No single protocol result can define all runners time-to-recovery

sources.title: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
sources.population_design_dose: 137 systematic reviews of randomized healthy-adult RT interventions,6-52 weeks; literature search October2024. General strength, hypertrophy, function and power outcomes.
sources.findings: Progressive RT with goal-specific variables is supported; many configurations work. Failure is not necessary; exact optimal set counts and individual response cannot be read from pooled summaries.
sources.locator: Eligibility; Tables3/6; Discussion and limitations lines900-924. Full text newly available in this round, unlike pilot abstract access.
limitations: Review overlap quantified only for strength; variable-level overview not comparison of all compound programs
Group-level general adult evidence does not certify an individual dose, clinical clearance, or specialized concurrent/taper program
counterevidence: More volume may improve some outcomes; omitted work is not assumed equivalent
Specificity and goal change can make a convenient substitute inadequate

sources.title: Acute Neuromuscular, Physiological and Performance Responses After Strength Training in Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: de Carvalho e Silva GI et al.
sources.population_design_dose: 19 qualitative/13 meta-analyzed studies of runners after resistance exercise; heterogeneous strength protocols, tasks and assessment times.

sources.title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.population_design_dose: 43 controlled studies; healthy adults; supervised concurrent training >=4 weeks vs identical strength alone. Chronic strength, explosive strength and hypertrophy, not next-morning readiness.
sources.findings: Pooled maximal strength and hypertrophy did not show clear attenuation; explosive-strength attenuation was present, especially close/session combinations. No universal compatibility or spacing claim follows.
sources.locator: Abstract Methods/Results; Discussion sections on explosive strength and limitations; publisher lines185-214.
limitations: Mostly medium/low methodological quality; intensity not consistently reported
Active training status pooled broadly; chronic group estimates cannot identify acute individual adequacy
counterevidence: L04 finds endpoint/subgroup attenuation under different definitions
No order-specific pooled effect established here; same-session power exception matters

sources.title: Acute Neuromuscular, Physiological and Performance Responses After Strength Training in Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: de Carvalho e Silva GI et al.
sources.population_design_dose: 19 qualitative/13 meta-analyzed studies of runners after resistance exercise; heterogeneous strength protocols, tasks and assessment times.
sources.findings: Acute peak torque and subjective/muscle-damage measures could worsen while several submaximal running physiological outcomes showed little change. Task and dose matter.
sources.locator: Results; Discussion including protocol contrasts; limitations and practical implications, publisher lines198-211.
limitations: Too few studies for robust 6/10/24/48h recovery curve
Does not quantify cost of the exact squat/RDL/split or guarantee a reduced set restores performance
counterevidence: Some submaximal tasks not impaired; reducing every lower/run pairing is unjustified
No single protocol result can define all runners time-to-recovery

sources.title: Concurrent Strength and Endurance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on the Impact of Sex and Training Status
sources.authors: Huiberts RO, Wust RCI, van der Zwaard S
sources.population_design_dose: 59 studies/1346 healthy adults18-50, concurrent >=4 weeks; strength/endurance training status classified separately. Online2023, issue2024.

sources.locator: Methods2.2-2.6; Results3.1/3.4/3.5; Discussion.
limitations: Mostly untrained strength participants; limited highly trained endurance evidence

Not an individual prediction or automatic priority policy

sources.title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.population_design_dose: 43 controlled studies; healthy adults; supervised concurrent training >=4 weeks vs identical strength alone. Chronic strength, explosive strength and hypertrophy, not next-morning readiness.
sources.findings: Pooled maximal strength and hypertrophy did not show clear attenuation; explosive-strength attenuation was present, especially close/session combinations. No universal compatibility or spacing claim follows.
sources.locator: Abstract Methods/Results; Discussion sections on explosive strength and limitations; publisher lines185-214.
limitations: Mostly medium/low methodological quality; intensity not consistently reported
Active training status pooled broadly; chronic group estimates cannot identify acute individual adequacy
counterevidence: L04 finds endpoint/subgroup attenuation under different definitions
No order-specific pooled effect established here; same-session power exception matters

sources.title: Acute Neuromuscular, Physiological and Performance Responses After Strength Training in Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: de Carvalho e Silva GI et al.
sources.population_design_dose: 19 qualitative/13 meta-analyzed studies of runners after resistance exercise; heterogeneous strength protocols, tasks and assessment times.
sources.findings: Acute peak torque and subjective/muscle-damage measures could worsen while several submaximal running physiological outcomes showed little change. Task and dose matter.
sources.locator: Results; Discussion including protocol contrasts; limitations and practical implications, publisher lines198-211.
limitations: Too few studies for robust 6/10/24/48h recovery curve
Does not quantify cost of the exact squat/RDL/split or guarantee a reduced set restores performance
counterevidence: Some submaximal tasks not impaired; reducing every lower/run pairing is unjustified
No single protocol result can define all runners time-to-recovery

sources.locator: Methods2.2-2.6; Results3.1/3.4/3.5; Discussion.

sources.title: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews
sources.population_design_dose: 137 systematic reviews of randomized healthy-adult RT interventions,6-52 weeks; literature search October2024. General strength, hypertrophy, function and power outcomes.
sources.findings: Progressive RT with goal-specific variables is supported; many configurations work. Failure is not necessary; exact optimal set counts and individual response cannot be read from pooled summaries.
sources.locator: Eligibility; Tables3/6; Discussion and limitations lines900-924. Full text newly available in this round, unlike pilot abstract access.
limitations: Review overlap quantified only for strength; variable-level overview not comparison of all compound programs
Group-level general adult evidence does not certify an individual dose, clinical clearance, or specialized concurrent/taper program
counterevidence: More volume may improve some outcomes; omitted work is not assumed equivalent
Specificity and goal change can make a convenient substitute inadequate

sources.title: Compatibility of Concurrent Aerobic and Strength Training for Skeletal Muscle Size and Function: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.population_design_dose: 43 controlled studies; healthy adults; supervised concurrent training >=4 weeks vs identical strength alone. Chronic strength, explosive strength and hypertrophy, not next-morning readiness.
sources.findings: Pooled maximal strength and hypertrophy did not show clear attenuation; explosive-strength attenuation was present, especially close/session combinations. No universal compatibility or spacing claim follows.
sources.locator: Abstract Methods/Results; Discussion sections on explosive strength and limitations; publisher lines185-214.
limitations: Mostly medium/low methodological quality; intensity not consistently reported
Active training status pooled broadly; chronic group estimates cannot identify acute individual adequacy
counterevidence: L04 finds endpoint/subgroup attenuation under different definitions
No order-specific pooled effect established here; same-session power exception matters

sources.authors: Wang Z, Wang YT, Gao W, Zhong Y

sources.findings: Tapering can improve endurance time-trial outcomes; moderator estimates are not a universal taper recipe. Competition-specific and concurrent-strength doses remain individual questions.
sources.locator: Eligibility criteria; Table1; Results/Table2; Limitations and conclusion.
limitations: FewRCTs; mostly men; limited training-status comparison
Specialized well-trained endurance evidence not all recreational adults
No exact combined10 kmstrength taper validated
counterevidence: Some moderators inconsistent; no universal41-60% reduction or<=21day command
Race cancellation/postponement changes intent, not automatic restoration of old workload

sources.title: Acute Neuromuscular, Physiological and Performance Responses After Strength Training in Runners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
sources.authors: de Carvalho e Silva GI et al.
sources.population_design_dose: 19 qualitative/13 meta-analyzed studies of runners after resistance exercise; heterogeneous strength protocols, tasks and assessment times.
sources.findings: Acute peak torque and subjective/muscle-damage measures could worsen while several submaximal running physiological outcomes showed little change. Task and dose matter.
sources.locator: Results; Discussion including protocol contrasts; limitations and practical implications, publisher lines198-211.
limitations: Too few studies for robust 6/10/24/48h recovery curve
Does not quantify cost of the exact squat/RDL/split or guarantee a reduced set restores performance
counterevidence: Some submaximal tasks not impaired; reducing every lower/run pairing is unjustified
No single protocol result can define all runners time-to-recovery
